s1.syndrome_frame: chronic foot pain with soft-tissue nodules and nerve involvement
salient_findings: pain in the plantar aspect of the left foot
three prominent, soft-tissue nodules with swelling and tenderness
numbness in the medial distal plantar foot
key_facts: 19-year-old woman
18-month history of pain in the plantar aspect of her left foot
pain was moderate initially and worsened at night
pain was exacerbated by compression and exposure to cold
three soft-tissue nodules were palpated in the plantar aspect of the left foot
nodules were mobile and not adherent to surrounding tissue
sensation testing revealed numbness in the medial distal plantar foot
toe and foot motor strength were normal
magnetic resonance imaging showed three nodules in the mid-plantar region
lesions were homogeneously isointense to skeletal muscle on T1-weighted images
lesions were homogeneously hyperintense without cystic degeneration on T2-weighted fat-suppressed images
lesions followed the course of branches of the common plantar digital nerves

shortlist.label: plexiform schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: multiple soft-tissue nodules with nerve involvement and characteristic 'mouse-tail' sign on MRI

shortlist.label: glomus tumor
shortlist.why_kept: pain exacerbated by compression and exposure to cold, and presence of soft-tissue nodules

shortlist.label: neurofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: multiple soft-tissue nodules and nerve involvement, although less likely given the absence of family history of neurofibromatosis

shortlist.label: schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: soft-tissue nodules with nerve involvement and characteristic MRI findings

shortlist.label: neurilemmoma
shortlist.why_kept: alternative term for schwannoma, with similar clinical and imaging characteristics

raw.rationale: The clinical presentation of multiple soft-tissue nodules in the plantar aspect of the foot, worsening pain at night, and numbness, combined with the imaging findings of multiple nodules following the course of branches of the common plantar digital nerves, is most consistent with plexiform schwannoma.

rejected.label: glomus tumor
rejected.why: Glomus tumors typically present with intense pain, temperature sensitivity, and are often located under the fingernail, which does not match this patient's presentation.

rejected.label: neurofibroma
rejected.why: Neurofibromas can occur anywhere, but the specific pattern of multiple nodules along the course of nerves and the imaging characteristics are more suggestive of schwannoma.

rejected.label: schwannoma
rejected.why: While schwannoma is a possible diagnosis, the presence of multiple nodules (plexiform) makes plexiform schwannoma a more specific and fitting diagnosis.

rejected.label: neurilemmoma
rejected.why: Neurilemmoma is another term for schwannoma, but the plexiform nature of the lesions points towards plexiform schwannoma as the more accurate diagnosis.
